title: How to Crack FAANG Interviews
content:
Cracking FAANG (Facebook/Meta, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, Google) interviews requires systematic preparation:

1. DATA STRUCTURES & ALGORITHMS: Master arrays, strings, linked lists, trees, graphs, heaps, tries, and dynamic programming. Use LeetCode — target 200+ problems. Focus on Medium difficulty. Use Neetcode 150 as your main guide.

2. SYSTEM DESIGN: Study scalable system architectures. Learn about load balancers, CDNs, databases (SQL vs NoSQL), caching (Redis, Memcached), message queues (Kafka), microservices, and API design. Practice designing Twitter, Uber, Netflix, WhatsApp, TinyURL.

3. BEHAVIORAL INTERVIEWS: Use the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result). Prepare 5-6 strong stories covering leadership, conflict resolution, failure/learning, cross-functional collaboration, and impact. Amazon focuses heavily on their 16 Leadership Principles.

4. TIMELINE: 3-6 month preparation for freshers, 2-3 months for experienced with strong DSA base.

5. SALARY: FAANG offers are 30-100% above market. Senior SDE at Google India: 80-200+ LPA total comp.

6. REFERRALS: A referral increases your interview chance by 3-5x. Connect with employees on LinkedIn and ask directly.

title: LinkedIn Profile Optimization Guide
content:
LinkedIn is the #1 professional network. Here's how to optimize your profile for maximum visibility:

1. HEADLINE: Don't just put your job title. Use keywords: 'Software Engineer | Python | FastAPI | Building @HireNexus'.

2. ABOUT: Tell your story in 3 paragraphs — who you are, what you do, what you're looking for. Include keywords naturally.

3. EXPERIENCE: Same as resume — action verbs, quantified achievements. Add media (screenshots, links).

4. SKILLS: List 50 skills. Get endorsements from colleagues. These influence LinkedIn search ranking.

5. OPEN TO WORK: Enable this privately so only recruiters see it. Choose your preferred roles and locations.

6. CONNECTIONS: Connect with people from target companies. Send personalized connection requests (100 chars).

7. CONTENT: Post 1-2 times per week. Share learnings, project updates, opinions. This builds visibility.

8. RECOMMENDATIONS: Ask 2-3 colleagues or managers to write recommendations. These build strong social proof.

title: Career Transition into Tech — Complete Guide
content:
Switching careers into tech is achievable in 6-12 months with the right approach:

1. CHOOSE YOUR PATH: Based on your background — Non-technical → Web Dev or QA; Finance → Data Science; Design → UI/UX → Frontend; Management → Product Manager; Science → ML/Data Science.

2. LEARN EFFICIENTLY: Pick one learning platform (Coursera, Udemy, freeCodeCamp). Don't hop between resources. Focus: 2-3 hours daily. Build projects immediately after each concept.

3. BUILD YOUR PORTFOLIO: 3-5 real projects with GitHub links. Ideas: todo app (too generic), instead build a job tracker, expense splitter, recipe meal planner with AI.

4. LEVERAGE YOUR OLD CAREER: Your domain knowledge is a superpower. Finance → FinTech, Healthcare → HealthTech, Retail → E-commerce. Use it to get roles where you combine industry + tech knowledge.

5. NETWORKING: Join communities (Discord servers, Twitter tech community, local meetups). Most career-switcher jobs come through network referrals, not cold applications.

6. REALISTIC TIMELINE: 6 months minimum for web dev. 12 months for data science. Be patient — the payoff is worth it.

SALARY EXPECTATION: Expect a 10-20% pay cut initially. Within 2-3 years in tech you'll surpass your old salary.

title: The Art of Salary Negotiation — Complete Playbook
content:
Salary negotiation is a skill that can make a 10-30% difference in your offer. Never skip it.

BEFORE THE OFFER:
- Research salary ranges: Glassdoor, LinkedIn Salary, Levels.fyi, AmbitionBox (India).
- Know your BATNA (Best Alternative to Negotiated Agreement) — another offer is your best leverage.
- NEVER reveal your current salary. Say: 'I'd prefer to focus on what the role is worth and what fits your budget.'

RECEIVING THE OFFER:
- Always ask: 'Is there any flexibility in the compensation package?'
- Get the offer in writing before negotiating.
- Express enthusiasm first: 'I'm really excited about this opportunity.'

NEGOTIATING:
- Counter with a specific number, not a range. Say 15L, not 12-15L.
- Justify with data: 'Based on my research and similar roles in this market, I was expecting X.'
- Negotiate total comp: base + bonus + ESOPs + joining bonus + annual hike cycle.

WHEN THEY SAY NO:
- Ask for a sign-on bonus instead: 'Can we offset the difference with a joining bonus?'
- Ask for earlier performance review: 'Can we schedule a review in 6 months instead of annually?'

INDIA-SPECIFIC: For 3-6 LPA roles, 5-10% negotiation is typical. For 10+ LPA, 15-25% is possible with competing offers.

title: Open Source Contribution Guide for Students
content:
Contributing to open source is the fastest way to build credibility as a developer:

1. WHERE TO START: GitHub — search for repos with labels 'good first issue', 'help wanted', 'beginner friendly'. Popular beginner-friendly projects: VS Code, React, FastAPI, freeCodeCamp, Hacktoberfest participants.

2. HOW TO CONTRIBUTE:
   a) Read CONTRIBUTING.md carefully
   b) Fork the repository
   c) Create a feature branch: git checkout -b fix/your-fix
   d) Make small, focused changes
   e) Write tests for your changes
   f) Submit a Pull Request with a clear description

3. PROGRAMS: Google Summer of Code (GSoC), Outreachy, MLH Fellowship, Hacktoberfest (October every year) — these programs pay stipends and look excellent on a resume.

4. BENEFITS: GitHub activity graph, exposure to production codebases, strong portfolio, mentorship from maintainers, possible job offers from the companies behind the projects.

5. GETTING MERGED: Be patient. Respond to review comments quickly. Be respectful. Start with small PRs.

title: Remote Job Search Strategy — India to Global
content:
Landing a remote job, especially with US/European companies from India, can 5-10x your salary:

1. BEST PLATFORMS FOR REMOTE JOBS:
   - Remote.com, We Work Remotely, Remotive.io, Turing.com
   - Arc.dev (vetted developers, get matched to companies)
   - Toptal (top 3% developers, high rates)
   - Upwork + Fiverr (freelance to start)
   - LinkedIn (filter by Remote in location)

2. PREPARATION: Remote companies value async communication skills, strong written English, self-management, and proof of work. Your GitHub and portfolio are MORE important than your degree.

3. SALARY EXPECTATIONS:
   - US startup remote: $40-100K/year (junior to senior)
   - European remote: €30-80K/year
   - These are 3-8x the equivalent Indian salary

4. LEGAL: You'll work as a freelancer/contractor initially. Handle taxes yourself (consult a CA). LUT filing required for GST exemption on export services.

5. TIMEZONE: Most US companies are fine with IST overlap of 4-6 hours (afternoon IST = morning US East Coast).

title: How to Build a Standout Portfolio
content:
Your portfolio is your most powerful job application tool — more important than your resume.

WHAT MAKES A GREAT PROJECT:
- Solves a Real Problem: Not another todo app. Build something you or others would actually use.
- Has Real Users: Even 10 users is impressive. Deploy it and share it.
- Shows Technical Depth: Not just CRUD. Add authentication, real-time features, AI integration, or performance optimizations.
- Has Good Documentation: README with setup instructions, screenshots, demo video.

PROJECT IDEAS BY ROLE:
- Frontend: AI image generator, real-time collaboration tool, job tracking dashboard
- Backend: URL shortener with analytics, payment integration, REST API with rate limiting
- Full Stack: SaaS boilerplate, job board with AI matching, e-learning platform
- ML: Stock price predictor, sentiment analyzer, recommendation system, RAG chatbot

HOW TO PRESENT:
1. GitHub repo with clean code and good commit history
2. Live demo (Vercel/Railway/Render is free)
3. 90-second demo video (even a screen recording)
4. Case study in your README: Problem → Solution → Tech stack → Challenges → Results

QUANTITY VS QUALITY: 3 excellent projects beat 10 basic ones every time.

title: The Complete Interview Day Guide
content:
Day-of interview preparation matters as much as months of study:

BEFORE THE INTERVIEW (night before):
- Review your resume — know every project, every number, every tech choice
- Research the company: product, tech stack, recent news, Glassdoor reviews
- Prepare 5 questions to ask the interviewer
- Lay out your clothes, test your internet (virtual), or plan your route (in-person)

THE CODING ROUND:
1. Repeat the problem in your own words to confirm understanding
2. Clarify edge cases: null inputs, empty arrays, large numbers
3. Think aloud — say what you're considering before writing code
4. Start with brute force, then optimize
5. Test with examples before saying you're done

THE BEHAVIORAL ROUND:
- Use STAR format for every answer
- Be specific — real numbers, real situations
- Common questions: 'Tell me about yourself', 'Why this company?', 'Biggest weakness?', 'Conflict with a colleague?', 'Most proud of?'

QUESTIONS TO ASK THE INTERVIEWER:
- 'What does the tech stack look like?'
- 'What does a typical sprint look like?'
- 'What are the biggest technical challenges the team faces?'
- 'What does success look like in the first 6 months?'

AFTER THE INTERVIEW:
- Send a thank-you email within 24 hours
- Follow up after 5-7 days if no response

title: Certifications Worth Getting in Tech (2025)
content:
The right certifications can make your resume stand out and prove skills to employers:

CLOUD:
- AWS Solutions Architect Associate: Most in-demand, 12,000+ jobs in India. Cost: ₹15,000
- Google Cloud Professional: Growing fast, especially for ML workloads
- Azure Fundamentals: Good for enterprise/Microsoft shops

DATA & AI:
- Google TensorFlow Developer Certificate: Validates ML implementation skills
- IBM Data Science Professional (Coursera): Beginner-friendly, affordable
- Databricks Certified Associate: High demand for data engineering roles

SECURITY:
- CompTIA Security+: Entry-level, widely recognized
- CEH (Certified Ethical Hacker): Good for security testing roles
- OSCP: Gold standard for penetration testers

WEB/PROGRAMMING:
- Meta Front-End Developer (Coursera): Structured curriculum, Meta-backed
- MongoDB Certified Developer: Good for MEAN/MERN stack developers

FREE CERTIFICATIONS:
- Google's free certifications (Grow with Google)
- HackerRank skill certifications
- freeCodeCamp certifications

IMPORTANT: Certifications supplement experience — they don't replace projects and real skills. Don't spend months on certifications instead of building.

title: Work-Life Balance and Avoiding Burnout in Tech
content:
Tech careers can be intense. Here's how to succeed without burning out:

SIGNS OF BURNOUT: Dreading work on Sunday nights, loss of creativity, constant fatigue, feeling cynical about your work, declining performance.

PREVENTION STRATEGIES:
1. SET BOUNDARIES: Define working hours and stick to them. Disable Slack/work notifications after hours.
2. TAKE REAL BREAKS: Use your vacation days. Step away from screens during lunch.
3. PHYSICAL HEALTH: Exercise 3x/week minimum. This is non-negotiable for mental clarity.
4. LEARN OUTSIDE WORK: If your job isn't teaching you, study on your own but protect personal time too.
5. TALK ABOUT IT: Find a mentor or peer group. Burnout is a systemic issue in tech — you're not alone.

COMPANY RED FLAGS TO AVOID:
- Constant 'crunch mode' treated as normal
- No mental health benefits
- On-call without compensation
- Senior engineers leaving frequently (check Glassdoor)

REMOTE WORK SPECIFIC: Create a dedicated workspace. End your 'commute' with a walk. Over-communicate your work to compensate for reduced visibility.
